content: The apex beat, also known as the point of maximum impulse (PMI), is the most outward and downward point from the sternum where the cardiac impulse can be felt. This impulse is generated by the heart as it rotates, moves forward, and strikes the chest wall during systole. Under normal circumstances, the apex beat can be palpated in the left fifth intercostal space, at the intersection with the left midclavicular line. In children, however, the apex beat is typically located in the fourth intercostal space, medial to the nipple. In some cases, the apex beat may be found in abnormal locations. For example, in individuals with dextrocardia, the apex beat may be felt on the right side of the chest. A lateral and/or inferior displacement of the apex beat is often indicative of an enlarged heart, a condition known as cardiomegaly. The apex beat can also be displaced by other conditions, such as pleural or pulmonary diseases, deformities of the chest wall, or abnormalities of the thoracic vertebrae. In certain situations, the apex beat may not be palpable at all. This can occur in individuals with a thick chest wall or in conditions where the stroke volume is reduced, such as during ventricular tachycardia or shock.
